utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm the doctor seeing you today. I understand you've been having burning when you pass urine since yesterday, and you're worried it might be a UTI. Can you tell me a bit more about what's been happening?
reply: It started yesterday morning, so about a day and a half ago. It stings and burns, and it is worst right at the end of weeing, just like my last one. I am going constantly, about every half hour, and only a little bit comes out and I have to rush. It is a bit cloudy and smells, but I have not seen any blood.

reply: No fevers or shivers and I feel fine apart from this, and I have nothing in my back except a bit of an ache low down in my tummy. I am eating normally and have not been sick.

utterance: Any unusual vaginal discharge, itch, or pain during sex? Are you currently sexually active, and when was your last period?
reply: No, nothing like that, and pain during sex has never been a problem. I do have a boyfriend I have been with for about a year and it is just him, and my last period was about two weeks ago and was normal.

utterance: Have you missed any contraceptive pills recently, or had any unprotected sex? And have you had urinary infections before — how many, and when was the last one?
reply: I am on the pill and I do not miss it, and we had been together the night before it started. I have had one urinary infection about two years ago, and that is it.

utterance: Just a couple more things so I can choose the right treatment. Do you have any kidney problems, diabetes, or problems with your immune system? Any allergies to antibiotics, and are you taking any other medicines or supplements besides the pill?
reply: No, I do not have anything like that, and I am not allergic to anything that I know of. I take the combined oral contraceptive pill.

utterance: From what you've told me and from the urine test, this looks like a straightforward bladder infection, which is a common type of urinary tract infection. The urine showed signs of infection, and you don't have fever or kidney pain, so it doesn't look like it's gone up to the kidneys.
reply: Oh, great. Can I just get the script now so I can head back to work?

awards.label: First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance: Yes, I've written a script for trimethoprim, one 300 mg tablet once a day for 3 days. Start today and finish all three tablets even if you feel better sooner. Most people start to improve within a day or two. It is fine to keep taking your pill as usual with this antibiotic. If you have vomiting or bad diarrhoea, the pill might not be absorbed properly, so use condoms as well until you have taken seven active pills in a row after that settles. Drink plenty of water, go to the toilet when you need to, and wiping front to back can help. Peeing after sex can lower the chance of another infection. You can take paracetamol if the burning or tummy ache is uncomfortable. Please come back, or go to an emergency department if you feel worse, if you get fever, shivers, pain in your back or sides, vomiting, you can't keep fluids down, you see a lot of blood in the urine, or you're not clearly better after two days. If this keeps coming back, we can look into it further. Does that all make sense, and do you have any questions?
reply: That all makes sense, thank you. I will just grab these and head back to the cafe now.
